title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 126
paragraphs: In these parts there are many lions and many wild oxen, the kind with the very large horns that are often brought into Greece. The range of these lions is bounded on one side by the Nestus, which flows through Abdera, and on the other by the Achelous, which flows through Acarnania: you will not see a lion in any part of Europe east of the Nestus, nor in the remaining part of the continent west of the Achelous. They are found only in the space between these rivers.
